newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends losses on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends losses on mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices extended their losses Monday, falling about 40 cents under February indices as normal to above-normal temperatures stretched across most of the U.S., market sources said.
February swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes continued to fall into the $2.40s, down about 30 cents from Friday.

The mild weather also took its toll on south Texas prices where traders reported closing deals in the $2.20s and $2.30s on Texas Eastern and Tennessee, down more than 25 cents on the day and down about 40 cents from index levels.
With temperatures expected to average about four to eight degrees F above normal this week in the East, prices at New York city-gate lost about 45 cents to the $2.90-3.20 range.
On the Appalachian pipes, the weakening Gulf prices pressured prices by another 30 cents to the $2.60s and $2.70s, falling an average of 40 cents from monthly indices.
Longer term forecasts from Weather Express Inc indicated colder temperatures in the eastern U.S. next week, with freezing weather possible as far south as Florida.
In the Midcontinent, February prices dropped another 20 cents to about $2.40 early and then $2.20s late, with Demarcation quoted in the $2.36-2.42 range.
Most of the Midwest is anticipating the arrival of cooler temperatures by Wednesday, Weather Services Corp said.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the $2.80-2.95 range, down about 30 cents from Friday.
In west Texas, where temperatures continue to hover slightly above normal, Permian prices eased into the $2.20s to low-$2.30s, down nearly 10 cents.
Swing prices at the southern California border were in the $2.50s early but then cratered to a low of $2.30 shortly before nomination deadlines.
